rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a Day-5 expanded blastocyst and the reported 3AA grade, but relies on cautious generic descriptors and includes uncertain image-based claims about TE prominence and possible collapse/granulation without strong support.
Integrates age, BMI, ovarian reserve, endometrium, male factor, first-cycle status, and lifestyle factors well, with appropriate emphasis on BMI as the main negative modifier.
Overall logical and internally consistent, with prognosis tied to embryo quality and patient factors; minor issues include some speculative comments and slightly shifting probability framing.

Recommendations are broadly consistent with IVF practice: SET favored, PGT-A not mandatory at age 34 in first cycle, caution about obesity and alcohol, and not overinterpreting one failed transfer. Minor deviations include some speculative future stimulation/adjuvant suggestions.
Provides practical next steps for transfer, luteal support, lifestyle optimization, and future-cycle review, though some recommendations remain somewhat general rather than protocol-specific.
